players.product: industrial & electronics gases (N2, He, specialty) for fabs

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 results (CFO Melissa Schaeffer / CEO Eduardo Menezes): sales up 9% and operating income up 19% on volume, currency and lower costs, partly offset by helium price headwind; EPS of $3.20 up 19% and above the top of the guidance range on stronger on-site volume and better-than-expected helium volume from space launches; operating margin 23.7% (expanded over 200 basis points); return on capital 11.4%. Volume growth came partly from new assets coming on stream in Asia; Asia segment operating income grew 25%.
quarterly_data.figure: sales up 9%; operating income up 19%; EPS $3.20 increased 19%; operating margin 23.7%; Asia operating income grew 25%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised: fiscal full-year EPS guidance raised to $13 to $13.25 (8% to 10% growth), driven by pricing actions, productivity and new asset contributions, with a more favorable second half expected for volumes in refining, electronics and aerospace; Q3 EPS expected at $3.25 to $3.35 (5% to 8% growth); capex guidance maintained at approximately $4 billion for the fiscal year (on track to cut capital spend by more than $1 billion vs prior year). Management kept its prior second-half assumptions because of Middle East conflict uncertainty; two new assets will contribute in the back half.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 EPS $13 to $13.25 (8% to 10%); Q3 EPS $3.25 to $3.35 (5% to 8%); capex approximately $4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics project pipeline: Air Products is currently executing approximately $1 billion in ASU and hydrogen projects in Asia for several multiphase projects serving semiconductor and memory customers, and expects to add another $1.5 billion to $2 billion to backlog in the next 6 months, including the newly announced Samsung advanced-fab project in South Korea. Total backlog is $9 billion; the traditional industrial gas backlog (excluding NEOM, Darrow and other non-profit-contributing projects) is a little over 2.5 (billion), a significant portion of it in electronics.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $1 billion electronics ASU/hydrogen projects in execution; $1.5 billion to $2 billion to be added to backlog in next 6 months; backlog $9 billion; traditional backlog a little over 2.5

quarterly_data.signal: AI-driven semiconductor super cycle: CEO says the industry is in the midst of a historical super cycle to satisfy AI demands with record capex projected between now and 2030, generating expansion opportunities for industrial gas providers; he has seen numbers in excess of $0.5 trillion of capex being spent by semiconductor and memory manufacturers, and electronics is benefiting from increased volumes due to a new asset onstream this year. CFO: very bullish on electronics over the next couple of years through the hyper cycle; electronics projects could quickly replace capital that was earmarked for the Darrow project, whose base case is not moving forward (go/no-go decision targeted by the middle of this calendar year).
quarterly_data.figure: in excess of $0.5 trillion of semiconductor and memory capex (as cited by management)

quarterly_data.signal: Helium supply disruption: Middle East events curtailed helium supply from Qatar (which represents 1/3 of the world's helium volume); the market, structurally long before the war, is now short. Air Products is covering customers from its dedicated Texas helium storage cavern (operational for nearly 5 years), multiple U.S. sources, its Sonatrach (Algeria) and Qatar Energy partnerships, and a Gardner Cryogenics ISO container fleet; the Qatar plant supplying it has been down since December. Constraints are moving product from Texas to Kansas (900 miles one way) and Kansas liquefaction capacity; the system is designed to cover one source being down, not the whole market.
quarterly_data.figure: Qatar = 1/3 of world helium volume; Texas cavern operational nearly 5 years

quarterly_data.signal: Helium to electronics: with long-term agreements signed during the last 6 months, Air Products expects helium volumes to large electronics customers in Asia to more than double between 2026 and 2030 (CEO later: expects it to be more than that). Helium agreements are on average between 3 and 5 years but recent agreements run longer as customers worry about supply reliability; helium price is still expected to be a headwind and to bottom by the end of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: helium volumes to large Asian electronics customers to more than double between 2026 and 2030; agreements on average between 3 and 5 years

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing: non-helium merchant pricing was up about 2% year over year (half in the Americas, half in Europe), while Asia non-helium pricing was largely flat; China remains a hypercompetitive market. Productivity: approximately $50 million in savings year-to-date from head count reduction; net debt-to-EBITDA 2.2x.
quarterly_data.figure: non-helium merchant pricing up about 2%; approximately $50 million savings year-to-date; net debt-to-EBITDA 2.2x

connects_to.relationship: industrial & specialty gas supply (build-own-operate) for Samsung advanced fab in South Korea

contracts.signal: Project announced the day before the call to build, own and operate multiple production facilities and specialty gas supply systems for a new advanced fab with Samsung in South Korea. CEO: the largest investment Air Products has ever made in electronics (amount not disclosed; he confirmed an analyst's comparison to a previous project was correct); probably the largest electronics site in the world; Air Products was the first supplier on Phase 1, this is the fifth phase, and volumes supplied under this agreement when completely built are approximately 3x larger than Phase 1; start of probably a 4-year construction.
contracts.units: fifth phase; volumes approximately 3x larger than Phase 1
contracts.value: not disclosed (largest investment ever made in the electronics side)
contracts.type: long-term build-own-operate industrial/specialty gas supply agreement
